title: VendPoint Start-Up Items: Demand Pattern Questions for Restock Teams
content:
Training questions on how the demand pattern of the item most recently added to a VendPoint Industrial Vending Program machine shapes its par in Corbett's start-up par review.

**What is the rule?** The item's demand pattern can replace the average per restock interval in the standard par, where the item's largest single vend is the largest number of units of the item issued in one vend on the machine at any time and its starter par is the par on its add entry: when the item's largest single vend is at least its average per restock interval, the larger of the average per restock interval and the largest single vend replaces it; when the largest single vend is below the average per restock interval and the item has fewer days in the machine than the settling period, the larger of two figures, the average per restock interval and the product of the starter par and one less the low-stock trigger fraction, replaces it; otherwise the average per restock interval stands.

**How long is the settling period?** 28 calendar days. The item's days in the machine are the calendar days from the date of its add entry to today, counted as one when the add entry is dated today.

**What is the low-stock trigger fraction?** The model's low-stock trigger percentage taken as a fraction of one hundred.

**Which records give the largest single vend?** Every vend of the item on the machine, at any time, not only the recent months.

### The three patterns

| Largest single vend against the average | Days in the machine | Figure that stands for the average per restock interval |
|---|---|---|
| At least the average | any | The larger of the average and the largest single vend |
| Below the average | fewer than 28 | The larger of the average and the starter par multiplied by one less the trigger fraction |
| Below the average | 28 or more | The average per restock interval |

### Hypothetical cases

Inputs are invented: an average per restock interval of 10 units, a 25% trigger.

- Largest single vend 12 units: 12 is at least 10, so the larger of 10 and 12, that is 12, stands in place of the average.
- Largest single vend 6 units, 20 days in the machine, starter par 20: 20 multiplied by 0.75 is 15; the larger of 10 and 15 is 15.
- Largest single vend 6 units, 28 days in the machine: the settling period has passed, and 10 stands.
- Largest single vend 6 units, 27 days in the machine, starter par 8: 8 multiplied by 0.75 is 6; the larger of 10 and 6 is 10.
